- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.15) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% in next 5–7 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% above recent mean), model often overshoots — cap forecast at +5% above prior peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.  
- If sentiment is positive (e.g., > 0.15) and model forecasts are rising, check for mean reversion — if price has been rising >3 days, reduce forecast slope by 10–15% for next 7 days.  
- When true outcome is consistently below forecast (especially in 3–5 day horizon), model exhibits “overconfidence bias” — adjust downward by 2–5% for next 3–5 days if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.  
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–0.10) and forecast is erratic, use 5-day rolling average to filter noise — ignore sharp spikes unless preceded by strong positive sentiment.  
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is >10% above true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, apply “mean reversion correction” — subtract 1–2% per day until forecast aligns with 10-day moving average.
